title: Note: reading a ghost story, part 1
summary: The first sentence of a spoken Japanese ghost story, taken apart with the structure from the earlier lessons.

blocks.text: This episode is a guided reading, made together with a Japanese storytelling channel, of a ghost story (怪談). Instead of teaching a new rule, it shows how to approach real material: stop at every sentence and ask what it is made of.

The story opens with それは, like English "It was ...". Japanese has no visible word for English "it" in this role. A zero pronoun does that job, so それ is really "that", a pointer to something the listener is about to learn. A story-opening of this kind sets the scene before any action starts.

items: Work through the story one sentence at a time.
Look for the engine and the main carriage first, including the invisible ones.
English "it" at the start of a story is usually a zero pronoun in Japanese.
Listen first, then analyze, then listen again.

blocks.text: Parts 2 and 3 continue the same story and look at more of its sentences.
